title: Compatible Artin--Schreier exact rows with coherent Frobenius models
statement: Let k and k′ be algebraically closed fields of characteristic p, p prime, with a k-algebra structure on k′. Let f:C to Spec k be a smooth proper connected curve of dimension at most one [def-sc-curves, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let C′ be its displayed base change. There are a finite-dimensional k-module V, Frobenius-semilinear F on V and F′ on k′ tensor V with F′(1 tensor v)=1 tensor F(v), abelian etale sheaves G on C and G′ on C′ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and short exact rows 0 to constant Z/p to G via i to G via wp to 0 and 0 to inverse-image constant Z/p to G′ via i′ to G′ via wp′ to 0 [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence, def-sc-constant-sheaves]. Their H^0(wp) and H^0(wp′) maps are surjective. There are a sheaf map q:inverse-image G to G′ and additive equivalences b:H^1(G) to V and b′:H^1(G′) to k′ tensor V [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], such that (inverse-image i) followed by q equals i′, b carries H^1(wp) to F-1, b′ carries H^1(wp′) to F′-1, and b′(H^1(q)(pullback(x)))=1 tensor b(x) for all x in H^1(G). No degree-one constant-sheaf kernel equivalence is asserted.

proof.text: Construct the lifted additive structure sheaves G and G′ and their Artin--Schreier exact rows. Identify the inverse image of the prime constant sheaf with the constant sheaf on C′, and transport its inclusion to i′. The structural ring map induces q. Both composites from the inverse-image constant sheaf to G′ send a prime-field section to the same constant function; the sheafification universal property gives (upperStar i) followed by q = i′.

Properness and smooth connectedness identify global functions with the algebraically closed field, and x^p-x is surjective on that field. Apply the degree-zero comparison, natural in wp, to obtain surjectivity of H^0(wp). The same argument applies to C′: properness and smoothness are stable under base change, and connectedness over an algebraically closed field is geometric connectedness. The Ext/derived comparison transports degree-zero epimorphy to the specified Sheaf.H model. The dimension-zero case is Spec k and obeys the same argument.

For dimension one, use the additive scalar model as V with its finite-dimensionality. Define F by the cohomology map of the sectionwise p-th-power endomorphism. For the scalar sheaf map mu_c, the equality mu_c followed by Frobenius = Frobenius followed by mu_(c^p) holds on all sections. Applying additive cohomology proves p-semilinearity. Additivity proves b(H^1(wp)(x))=F(b(x))-b(x). In dimension zero take V=H^1(C,O_C)=0; its unique Frobenius is semilinear.

Use flat coherent base change and the etale/Zariski comparison to construct b′:H^1(C′,G′) to k′ tensor V. In the finite affine-cover Cech complexes, scalar extension sends a cochain s to 1 tensor s and structure-ring pullback sends s^p to its pullback to the p-th power. The Cech comparisons commute with these additive maps; Frobenius need not be O-linear. Transport the induced Frobenius on C′ through b′ to F′. This gives semilinearity, F′(1 tensor v)=1 tensor F(v), the formula for wp′, and the canonical pullback formula b′(H^1(q)(pullback(x)))=1 tensor b(x). The same construction works for the zero module. No calculation of the kernel of F-1, and no invariance of fixed points, occurs in this step.
